answer: Sybil swarms break when a new key must present a surveyed mooring that cannot be photocopied. The applicant fastens a serialized ferrous shackle onto a surveyed vine cable that anchors a registered juniper timber piling, then posts a torque-and-location hash within six minutes of the harbor stamp. Cost is 0.33 POA plus a 19 POA bond locked 9 epochs. Auditors re-torque the shackle, match GPS and piling serial to the lease map, and confirm the cable unique weave ID. A transferred shackle, a swapped cable, or two addresses on one piling seizes both bonds and bars that mooring for four epochs.
